newsitem.title: USA: Maytag sets $70 mln stake in China venture.
newsitem.headline: Maytag sets $70 mln stake in China venture.

text.p: Maytag Corp said Monday it will invest about $70 million in a series of joint ventures in laundry and refrigeration with the Hefei Rongshida Group Corp in Hefei, Anhui Province, the People's Republic of China.
The joint ventures, which will operate under the name Hefei Rongshida, have received approval from the provincial government in Anhui, Maytag said in a statement.

Maytag will invest $35 million for an equity stake in three joint ventures with the Hefei Rongshida Group's established laundry products company and associated enterprises (motors, plastics, molds, and small appliances), known as "RSD." RSD is a widely recognized name brand in China.

In the second phase of the ventures, Maytag will provide refrigeration product design and engineering, and both Maytag and RSD will invest about $35 million each over the next several years to develop a refrigeration products business and build a refrigerator manufacturing facility in Hefei.

"I'm excited and pleased by this opportunity with RSD," said Maytag chairman Leonard Hadley, in a statement. "This is a focused investment for Maytag aimed at profitable growth in a market that is growing at double-digit rates."

Maytag will own 50.5 percent in the Hefei Rongshida joint ventures through two wholly owned subsidiaries (Maytag International Investments BV at 49.5 percent, and AERA Ltd, Hong Kong, at one percent). Hefei Rongshida Group Corp will own 49.5 percent. Maytag's involvement in the joint ventures will be managed by Maytag International Inc, headquartered in Chicago, which handles export sales, licensing, and international ventures for the corporation.
RSD's 1995 revenues were about $100 million, with operating margins in low double-digits. RSD produced about 1.1 million washing machines in 1995.

Available statistics indicate 9.5 million washing machines were produced in China in 1995, to serve a growing market significantly larger than the U.S. Manufacturers in the U.S., by comparison, produced 6.9 million washing machines in 1995. Maytag produces major appliances, floor care products, and cold-drink vending machines.
